questions.prompt: A calibration reports 0.2 px RMS reprojection error on the 300 corners it was fitted to. Which statement is justified?
options: Only that the model fits those points; you still need error on held-out views
The camera is accurate to 0.2 px everywhere in the image, including the corners
Any new image taken with this camera will have a 0.2 px error
The distortion model is correct, since the error is below a quarter pixel
questions.explanation: Fit error is measured on the data that chose the parameters; it is optimistic.

questions.prompt: Reprojection residuals (du, dv) in pixels: (1, 1), (2, 0), (0, -2). Compute the RMS error in pixels (precision 0.01).
A lens has k1 = -0.1, k2 = 0, f = 600 px. About how many pixels does a point at normalised radius 0.5 shift relative to the ideal pinhole, f*r*|k1|*r^2? (precision 0.1)
A 5x8-corner board is seen in 10 views. The model has 4 intrinsics, k1, k2 and 6 pose values per view. What is the ratio of scalar residuals to parameters? (precision 0.05)
All 20 calibration images show the board centred, parallel to the image plane at about 1 m. What is the main risk?
options: The RMS will be large because a flat board gives poorly conditioned corners
Focal length and distortion are poorly determined, although the RMS looks small
Corner detection fails on a frontal board, so most views are rejected
The principal point becomes exactly known, so the other parameters are certain
questions.explanation: Frontal central views do not separate focal length from distance and never probe the corners.

questions.prompt: Why is RMS preferred to the mean of the residual lengths when summarising reprojection error?
options: It weights large residuals more, so outliers are not hidden
It keeps the direction of the error, which the mean discards
It is always smaller, so the calibration looks better
It is measured in different units than the residuals
questions.explanation: Mean of lengths <= RMS; squaring penalises outliers.

questions.prompt: Describe how you would validate a new camera calibration before using it for ranging, including how you split data and what you would report.
rubric: Hold out whole views chosen before fitting; never use them in the fit.
Report training and held-out RMS in pixels, residual plot, and number/coverage of views.
Checks stability against a second session or datasheet focal length, and re-calibrates after lens changes.
questions.explanation: Rubric-guided: compare your answer with each rubric point; this question is not automatically graded.
